Key Activities: Coordinates and manages the activities of multi-disciplinary project teams, combining Statistics Canada and external resources, to evaluate the relevance and performance of programs, policies and initiatives, and to provide advice to the Evaluation Manager, the Director, the Chief Audit and Evaluation Executive, and senior management.

Consults with the Evaluation Manager and Statistics Canada program managers, in order to discuss and recommend project objectives, scope, approaches to be utilized, the timing and resources required for studies and projects and negotiates and secures agreement on courses of action and activities to be taken.

Initiates and coordinates complex studies and projects involving own and other government departments, partners and stakeholders; identifies project activities and study techniques to be applied; estimates human and financial resource requirements, and makes recommendations to the Evaluation Manager; schedules and assigns activities; coordinates and monitors work to ensure project objectives are met; and manages the design and adaptation of data collection tools for studies.

Plans, manages and coordinates economic and socio-economic analysis of Statistics Canada programs to evaluate their effectiveness against organizational strategic objectives and priorities. Manages the selection of methodologies for evaluation studies such as cost-benefit analysis, and manages the application of analytical tools, including qualitative and quantitative analysis of data.

Leads research to assess current and future requirements for statistical data; conducts analyses of conclusions on a broad and complex range of studies, and provides advice and recommendations to senior managers and subject-matter experts concerning changes or improvements to Statistics Canada policies, strategic plans, programs, and services as well as redesigns of programs based on studies conducted.

Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations, and provides advice and recommendations to the Evaluation Manager, Director, Chief Audit and Evaluation Executive and senior management to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.

Consults with representatives of OGDs, other levels of government, partners and stakeholders on studies and evaluation projects to be undertaken jointly (e.g., government-wide evaluations). Represents Statistics Canada and the Evaluation Division at meetings, on committees and working groups to discuss and share best practices, tools and approaches.
Provides input and data related to the development of the Statistics Canada Evaluation Plan, the Departmental Plan, Business Plan, Departmental Results, and other relevant departmental documents.

Communication:: Presentation and negotiation skills are required to secure the cooperation and buy-in of Statistics Canada managers on the establishment of the objectives, approaches, schedules, timing and resource requirements related to program evaluations and studies.

Oral and written skills are required to present and explain to all levels of management (e.g., manager through to Director General as well as senior management) conclusions from evaluations and other studies to gain acceptance of recommendations concerning changes or improvements to agency policies, plans, programs, and services as well as the redesign of programs based on studies conducted.

Oral presentation skills are required to explain to Statistics Canada program managers and staff, or project team members, issues related to evaluation processes, practices, plans and methodologies, result-based measurement, management, processes and practices, to obtain cooperation throughout the project phases.
Negotiation and consultation skills are needed when communicating with OGDs, partners and stakeholders to establish project / study requirements and parameters.

Consultation and liaison skills are required to establish and maintain a variety of networks within and outside of the Federal government to participate on departmental and interdepartmental committees, seminars, workshops and task forces with individuals from a variety of disciplines and knowledge levels. This involves discussing and resolving issues, working partnerships, gaining and maintaining the acceptance of members, and developing strong working relationships.

Communication skills are required to consult with officials from central agencies to exchange and negotiate the type of information required for program evaluation, to resolve problems, and present Statistics Canada’s viewpoint concerning service-wide program evaluation issues.

Writing skills are required to develop and prepare evaluation reports, papers, briefing materials, presentations, and correspondence. Oral and written skills are required to negotiate and manage contracts with external consultants.
Knowledge of Specialized Fields:: Knowledge of theories, principles, methodologies, standards, practices and tools associated with program evaluation, risk management and performance measurement. These are required to: plan, design and select the appropriate approaches and methodologies, definitional devices (logic models, comparative analyses, profiles and case studies), as well as data collection instruments (focus sessions, interviews, surveys) to conduct specific evaluations; determine relative strengths and weaknesses of the approaches; to plan, coordinate and manage program evaluation projects and studies; manage the application of techniques by project team members.

Knowledge of theories and principles of economics, sociology, social sciences, demography and statistics to: plan, direct and coordinate economic and socio-economic analysis of programs to evaluate their effectiveness against organizational strategic objectives; formulate and provide recommendations on agency policies, and direct the application of statistical and quantitative analysis. Knowledge of socio-economic trends in Canada and their impact on Statistics Canada programs.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research are required including: hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, and experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, interviews, focus groups, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis, including statistical sampling and cost-benefit analysis; computer assisted analytical packages. Knowledge of the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques are required in order to direct the application of project methodologies.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management related to human and financial resources to plan and coordinate the work of Statistics Canada evaluation teams, and agency/ interdepartmental project teams involved in the conduct of studies.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write reports, presentations, correspondence and other supporting materials and to determine and assess the design and content of reports that will be published.
Contextual Knowledge:: Knowledge of Statistics Canada’s structure, organization, mandate, vision, business lines, program structure, organizational hierarchy and priorities in order to: identify evaluation issues and manage program evaluations; direct the provision of meaningful results on individual evaluations; provide input to the strategic and operational business plans; and develop recommendations.

Knowledge of central agency policies and guidelines concerning program evaluation in order to recommend the objectives and approaches to program evaluations and negotiate with central agency officials concerning the information required for evaluation. Knowledge is required of policies, practices and guidelines related to central agencies and Parliament accountability and reporting requirements. This knowledge is required to recommend evaluation and performance measurement frameworks for Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of the Statistics Act to understand the legislative requirements under which the agency operates such as the need to ensure the confidentiality of all information provided to it.

Knowledge of other federal department programs that are affected by, or have an impact on Statistics Canada programs and policies in order to understand and evaluate the context in which Statistics Canada and its programs operate and to collaborate on, manage and coordinate inter-departmental evaluation studies and projects.

Knowledge of partners and stakeholders (including various provincial or territorial statistical organizations) who are affected by or who have an impact on departmental programs and policies to evaluate their impact on the agency, when managing and coordinating program evaluations.

Knowledge of emerging trends and developments in the Canadian private sector, academia and non-governmental organizations, as well as statistical programs of foreign governments in order to facilitate appropriate analysis.

Knowledge of government and departmental regulations, policies and legislation as they apply to evaluation program activities, issues, processes and methods. These include the Public Service Values and Ethics Code, the Policy on Results and its related directives and standards (Mandatory Procedures for Departmental Results Frameworks, Program Inventories, Performance Information Profiles and Programs, Mandatory Procedures for Evaluation, Standard on Evaluation, Standard on Mandatory Outcomes and Performance Indicators, Standard on Tagging), the Financial Administration Act, the Federal Accountability Act, Privacy and Access to Information Acts, Official Languages Act, Public Opinion Research and the Management Accountability Framework. This is required to understand the impact of legislation, regulations and interrelationships with other federal / provincial / territorial legislation.
Research and Analysis:: Directs the assessment and selection of methodologies (cost-benefit, comparative analysis) and analytical tools (statistical analysis, qualitative analysis) and makes recommendations on the scope and objectives of studies to the Evaluation Manager.

Manages the analysis and synthesis of information and data collected from a variety of sources and methods (surveys, interviews, literature reviews, program documentation, operational data, statistical databases and reports). Based on analyses, formulates conclusions on policy / program effectiveness and develops options and recommendations for improvement.

Designs, develops, tests, modifies and applies new data collection tools, techniques and methods (databases, questionnaires, surveys, case studies, self-assessment, interview, file review and project review guides) and performance measurement methods to meet requirements for unique / specialized projects.

Identifies sources of information required to support program evaluation and to develop, coordinate and maintain data on Statistics Canada programs. Identify and evaluate the extent to which factors, including social, economic and demographic trends have impacts on Statistics Canada programs and evaluation studies.

Reviews, evaluates and edits findings and conclusions of studies conducted by project teams and/or contractors for thoroughness, credibility, logic and validity; evaluates the appropriateness of recommendations and advice in an environment of changing priorities and resource constraints. Conclusions drawn and presented must also reconcile potentially differing views of stakeholders.

Key Activities: Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. This involves setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.

Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders (within the Agency, the federal, provincial-territorial or municipal governments and agencies, academia and international institutions and private organizations) in order to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.

Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.
Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.
Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.
Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.

Responsibility: Human Resources Responsibility
Human Resources Responsibility: Manages teams involved in the production, integration or analysis of data and/or leads project teams. Determines objectives and priorities and assesses the work requirements, schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives. This could involve recruitment activities, completion of employee performance evaluation or review of performance evaluations prepared by colleagues and approval of training plans. Present classification and staffing options to management and coordinate some human resources activities related to managing staff and leading a team.
Operational Responsibility: Responsible for promoting the development of new methods for collecting, modeling and processing data to meet program requirements and user needs.
Plans, coordinates and executes outreach activities and user consultations.
Coordinates activities including: gathering information from various sources, performing statistical analysis, interpreting and reporting on the intelligence obtained from data analysis.
Responsible for the development of recommendations and providing strategic advice to senior management in order to secure funding for projects and change strategies related to programs.
Analyzes current work performed by programs or other data sources, in order to add value by linking existing data and to expand analytical outputs.

Responsible for providing advisory and consultative services as well as subject matter advice to data users within and outside the Agency in order to maximize the accuracy and effectiveness of data products.
Responsible for making linkages across programs and divisions to leverage opportunities for further collaboration.
Responsible for the review and editing of analytical material for internal use or publication purposes.

Synthesizes complex statistical data from a wide range of sources to provide decision-makers at all levels of government, businesses, national economic agencies and academics, with information leading to decision making regarding a vast array of economic policies, programs and initiatives.
Skill: Knowledge and experience using various tools, techniques or software to evaluate, manipulate, , integrate, process, analyze and visualize data. This may include experience with machine learning and other skills related to big data.

In-depth knowledge of statistical principles, theories and practices, to conduct comprehensive analysis for the purpose of producing reliable and relevant statistical data, and to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program outputs, concepts and methods used.
Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods required to integrate and interpret data and to provide technical advice to other professionals.

Knowledge of project management principles, including developing project scope, budget, resource allocation, objectives, timelines, as well as mitigation strategies to address potential delays, issues and risks to overall project completion.
Knowledge of data sources, conceptual frameworks, and statistical methods to plan, evaluate, develop and lead new or existing programs (e.g. develop new methods, concepts, applications).

Ability to communicate efficiently orally and in writing (e.g. analytical material, briefing notes, presentations), to understand user needs, to identify data linkage opportunities, to interpret results and synthesize messages, and to negotiate, consult and liaise with stakeholders.
Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other relevant acts related to the subject matter areas, and of Statistics Canada policies.

Knowledge of statistical programs and products, including opportunities, limitations and potential policy impacts related to the area of expertise is required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to statistical programs if necessary.
Solid understanding of government key priorities and programs and the ability to interpret information needs relating to specific policies or programs of key partners.
Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and abroad as they relate to statistical programs and new data requirements.

Continuous learning of methods to integrate data from a variety of sources, evaluate the conceptual framework used and the compatibility of data with other programs, develop modifications or update program content and coverage and devise new classifications, concepts, definitions and operational procedures relating to area of expertise.

In-depth knowledge of horizontal topics, classification systems, concepts and international frameworks to integrate multiple data sources and ensure the overall coherence and soundness of the economic statistical program data produced.

Ability to interpret the relative quality of data produced, determine reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and economic conditions.

Positions.Position Title: Unit Head, Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation
Key Activities: Plans, develops, implements, directs and monitors statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems.

Determines changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations; and establishes short-term and long-term plans and priorities.

Identifies and researches trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata and the methods used to develop, manipulate, store, retrieve and disseminate statistical metadata in government and other organizations in order to plan, manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management processes and systems.

Provides input to the development and revision of policies, directives and guidelines relevant to statistical metadata quality; plans and directs metadata quality assessment projects and reviews; reports to senior management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata contained within corporate metadata systems and suggests means for improvements, if required.

Participates in, and leads, working groups, task forces and committees as an expert in the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager or Senior Advisor.

Manages a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams involved the development, production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and statistical metadata processes and systems. Manages the financial resources attached to each project.

Communication: Provides expert advice and specialized training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national and international organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures, methods and systems used in the management of statistical metadata. Provides direction with respect to establishing project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiating modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; and to suggesting improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Provides clear and comprehensible guidance, direction and specialized training to subordinate staff, colleagues, clients, systems specialists and management with respect to translating requirements for the management of statistical metadata into methods, procedures and systems specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain the rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.  When recommendations are challenged or misinterpreted, logical arguments are presented to defend the validity of the approaches used in order to maintain the division’s and Statistics Canada’s reputation for producing, storing and disseminating high quality metadata.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge on metadata management.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Extensive knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems.

Extensive knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems; to manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management processes and systems, and to lead metadata quality evaluations for surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of current and emerging trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management in Canada and internationally, in order to evaluate Statistics Canada’s statistical metadata management program in a broader context; to anticipate, understand needs for, plan, manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management methods, procedures and systems.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to interpret client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs; and to make recommendations to clients and managers with respect to possible enhanced approaches that could result in improved metadata quality.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to effectively manage financial resources, coordinate the activities of multi-disciplinary teams, manage performance, develop the skills, and competencies of team members. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.

Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and knowledge of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to inform the planning of resource allocation and long-term strategies for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
Contextual knowledge: Extensive knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada and internationally.

Extensive knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada and internationally.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs into a broader corporate metadata management system and to ensure the overall relevance, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata contained within corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada.

Extensive knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term and long-term priorities for the processing, storing and dissemination of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently plan and direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to senior management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret client requirements with respect to the production, storage and dissemination of metadata, to determine the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet the requirements of these clients and to translate client requirements into timely and affordable services. Clients are often uncertain of policy, procedural and systems restrictions and are unfamiliar with the options, methods and timelines required to produce and disseminate high quality metadata.

Reviews polices, guidelines, directives, methods, procedures and systems used for managing statistical metadata within Canada and internationally in order to determine the need for development, modification and adaptation of corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada. Statistical metadata management programs are often very complex and have been designed for specific purposes which must be evaluated when taking into consideration the feasibility of the various features of such programs and the potential impacts and results in terms of Statistics Canada’s priorities for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Analyses new methods, techniques and practices of managing statistical metadata and the associated costs and limitations. Identifies the availability of alternate means of producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata in order to evaluate the suitability of methods, procedures and systems with respect to the short-term and long-term program impacts and benefits.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and determines reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides senior management with interpretations and recommendations affecting policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used for the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata.

Key Activities: Plans, manages and conducts studies and/or projects using quantitative statistical data analysis methods, such as: data wrangling, validation, mining, and visualization (in R/RStudio, Python, SQL, Java, JavaScript or another software), as well as software development, application of machine/deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques to anticipate and solve complex business problems.

Plans, leads and identifies new opportunities for the acquisition, analysis and integration of large statistical data sets from a wide variety of structured and unstructured data sources to identify patterns and trends contributing to the development of solutions to complex business problems.

Plans, researches, leads and develops statistical measures and new data analysis techniques and processes, survey development, survey methodology, or components of data governance (e.g., policies, processes and standards, privacy, data quality, risk management) and on the use of data to optimize business value.

Plans and leads the assessment of the social, economic, fiscal implications of data to ensure that the development of policies, strategies, programs and other initiatives take into consideration the business foresight revealed from data analytics.
Plans and leads the ongoing tracking, monitoring and reporting of the performance of decision systems and accuracy of statistical models.

Advises and briefs project teams, colleagues, managers and senior managers on implications of studies conducted.  Drafts dashboards, briefing notes, reports, and presentations, and contributes to the development and evaluation of position and policy papers and ministerial correspondence and/or Cabinet documents.

Plans, coordinates and leads Departmental project teams/working groups and/or components of interdepartmental projects/working groups.  Formulates and recommends the nature, scope, analytical methods, objectives, terms of reference and resource requirements for research projects.  Manages resources assigned to studies and projects. Develops contracts and cost estimates to cover activities of projects. Negotiates contracts with consultants. Monitors contractor deliverables and recommends approval of invoices for payment.

Represents the Departmental position on data strategy, plans and initiatives in consultation and discussions on collaborative data science projects with partners including other government departments.

Builds client/stakeholder networks and provides technical expertise and leadership to federal government departments in matters relating to data science and analytics, to optimize business value of data, to determine the implications on policy and programs and the decision-making process.

Responsibility: Judgement and latitude are required to plan, manage and conduct economic, sociological and/or statistical projects, to analyse existing data science techniques, methods or approaches and to plan, develop and implement databases, and other analytical tools, approaches and methodologies.
There is a requirement to plan, manage/coordinate the work of unit analysts, and/or lead Departmental projects on a regular basis, as well as components of interdepartmental projects/working groups.

There is a requirement to provide advice and prepare briefing notes, discussion, position and policy papers, and presentations for senior managers, for use at Department and interdepartmental meetings. The purpose is to communicate results of analysis and studies and their implications relative to the development and/or assessment of new or enhanced policies, regulations, legislation or other initiatives.
There is also a requirement to manage, plan, design and develop data translation and exchange activities to support the sharing and use of data internally and externally.
This work affects data science activities undertaken by other analysts, multi-disciplinary working groups and/or project teams, and ultimately decisions and recommendations made by senior management.
Judgement to discuss business information without divulging confidential information.

Plans, manages/coordinates the work of unit analysts, and/or lead Departmental projects on a regular basis, as well as components of interdepartmental projects/working groups. This includes planning and scheduling work, establishing objectives, goals, priorities and milestones; resolving conflicting priorities, identifying human resources needs, determining/recommending appropriate selection methods (e.g. internal/external resources or contractors) to meet project objectives; evaluating performance; providing leadership as well as training and guidance to staff and project team members.
There may also be a requirement to analyse and provide cost estimates for the budgeting process.

Personal use and care of a computer and related software; standard office equipment, furnishings and supplies; reference material and policy documents; and multimedia equipment. May handle sensitive materials.
Uses taxi chits and travel credit cards for authorized business purposes.

Conceptualizes unique Data Science problems or challenges within the Department, leading and conducting comprehensive monitoring and data gathering to extract, integrate, synthesize, and analyze/assess vast amounts of complex data from multiple and diverse sources.

Conduct complex unique and non-recurring research studies and analysis; analyze and assess the current and future impact/effect of proposals, issues, and strategies; analyze and integrate innovative alternate approaches, positions, or external research findings for potential applicability; identify opportunities, formulate and modify strategies and positions, and; provide recommendations for final decision-making by senior management.

Produce and provide advice and guidance to all levels of government, business, and national agencies and academics, on statistical modelling results, methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in Data Science or related programs. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information into understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities pertaining to STATCAN’s mandate.
Define the nature and scope of Data Science projects and identify potential collaborators and beneficiaries of research.
This includes assessing net benefits and risks of proposed projects and evaluating potential new technologies.

Understand the resources, tools, and systems required to maintain and expand on Data Science products and systems on an ongoing or long-term basis, in order to develop strategies for and inform managers of what resources are needed to sustain, maintain, and support data science applications once they have been deployed.

Investigate client requirements for data projects, define the nature and scope of special studies, and determine the sources of data as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.
Develop guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications, and recommend modifications and improvements to existing procedures.

Initiative is required to identify new sources of information and study in order to maintain awareness of and emerging technologies and trends in Machine Learning and Al and their applications for relevant business ends.

Research, collect, and exploit information, and to develop, maintain, and implement information-related systems. This requires selecting, applying, and implementing correct analytical methodologies, techniques, and evaluation approaches; ensuring the quality and integrity of the information and data; and ensuring outputs, databases, and models meet client needs, and are transferred to the appropriate group for deployment, maintenance and supports.

Prepares technical, position and policy papers, briefing notes, and presentations which provide critical input regarding the economic and and Statistics implications of data science studies. Prepares reports to be submitted for publishing. This information is also used for planning and decision making for an array of key policies, programs, legislation and regulations by the Department and stakeholders.
Skill: Strong communication skills are required to establish, maintain and expand networks across the branch and the federal community of practice to share best practices in advanced analytics.
Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.

Strong writing skills are necessary to prepare and present clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for senior managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science. Information must be impartial and clearly presented to minimize the potential for misinterpretation.

Discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.

There is a requirement to liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development, and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.

Negotiating skills are required to: negotiate components of agreements concerning data science studies; negotiate mechanisms and components of research agreements with external partners including officials of other government departments.

The work requires in-depth knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, text mining, and qualitative analysis. This knowledge is required to optimize the use of the Statistics Canada’s data assets and to strengthen advanced analytics literacy. The work requires knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling that provides meaningful information for policy and program decisions by management.

In-depth knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.

In-depth data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data, including the knowledge needed to read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data, as well as understand the use of data in decision-making and data-driven problem solving. Advanced data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use. This is needed to formulate advice and recommendations on complex and sensitive issues/files.

In-depth knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research is required including; hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis including statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis; computer assisted analysis packages; and the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques in order to recommend and select project methodologies.

The work requires in-depth knowledge of project management practices, techniques and practices combined with practical experience in planning and developing project proposals, business cases, project plans, schedules and reports.

The work requires an in-depth knowledge of the mandate, vision, values, culture, organization, legislation, programs, business lines and operations of Statistics Canada.  This is needed to ensure the alignment of the data analytics strategy with the department’s business intelligence requirements.

The work requires in-depth knowledge of the machinery of government to provide strategic advice on policy and program development, to engage in the system of multi-jurisdictional relations and to advance information and Cabinet Committees; knowledge of the roles and responsibilities of central agencies and partner government departments to anticipate multi-dimensional issues, participate in multi-departmental and federal/client/stakeholder project teams, and enhance knowledge sharing; knowledge of domains affected by departmental decisions; and knowledge of the positions, interests, priorities, structure and key officials of other organizations to support their engagement by STATCAN officials.

The work requires in-depth knowledge and understanding of the governance structures of Statistics Canada’s partnerships in order to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.

Knowledge of Departmental, Central Agencies and Library and Archives Canada policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.

Key Activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program.
